name: Sanmachi Suji Old Town
tagline: Preserved Edo streets and sake breweries
description: The historic heart of Takayama, where dark wooden merchant houses, sake breweries and craft shops line narrow lanes beside the Miyagawa river. Atmospheric and touristy by day, it turns quiet and magical once the crowds thin each evening.
bestFor: Culture lovers wanting to live inside Takayama's iconic old-town streets

name: Takayama Station and City Centre
tagline: Convenient hub for transport and cafes
description: The practical modern core around Takayama Station, home to buses, trains, supermarkets, cafes and everyday services. It offers the town's best convenience and value, with laptop-friendly coffee shops and easy onward connections to Nagoya and the mountains.
bestFor: Remote workers who value transport links, cafes and daily convenience
cons: Less charm than the old town

name: Higashiyama Temple Walk District
description: A peaceful eastern quarter following the Higashiyama walking course past temples, shrines and quiet residential lanes. It offers a calm, spiritual counterpoint to the busy markets, with forested hillsides and gentle paths ideal for reflective morning walks.
bestFor: Those craving calm, greenery and a contemplative daily rhythm

name: Hida-no-Sato Outskirts
tagline: Residential calm near folk village and springs
description: The southwestern residential outskirts stretching toward the Hida folk village and hot-spring resorts. Greener and more spacious than the centre, it suits longer stays with affordable housing, mountain views and easy access to nature, though you will rely on buses or a bike.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads wanting space, nature and lower rents nearby
pros: Close to hot springs and Hida-no-Sato
